chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, from al-Zurari, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say:
There is no servant who commits a sin but that he is given respite from that morning until nightfall, so if he seeks forgiveness from Allah, it is not written against him.
ai.seo_question: How long does a sinner have to repent before their sin is recorded?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* highlights the divine mercy of a specific temporal window for repentance, emphasizing that immediate contrition can erase the record of sin entirely. It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the efficacy of *istighfar* (seeking forgiveness) before the next evening, encouraging believers to act swiftly rather than delaying their return to Allah.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 3.Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Zurārah who said, “I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh (a) say, ‘
There is no servant who commits a sin but that he is given respite from that morning until nightfall, so if he repents to Allah [within that time], it is not written against him.’”
